## Problem statement

The ring-timing CLI's operator-facing text report mixes per-seed and multi-seed
figures. `formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders:

- means over the seed set for `deployments`, `measured runs`, `total`, `banked salvage` and `ring secured`;
- but **seed 1's own value** for `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` (`report.runs[0]?.retryMinutes`, `runs[0]?.betweenSortieMinutes`, `runs[0]?.retakeMinutes` / `runs[0]?.expectedRetakes`).

With the default three-seed evidence set the two halves of one report therefore
describe different populations.

## Evidence

`npm run ring-timing` (2026-11-11, worktree of AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ, exit 0):

```text
Ring 2 · grind · seeds 1, 2, 3
  retries            55.0 min
  total              116.4 min (min 112.7, max 123.4)
```

The committed artefact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, revision
`e873e8c3`) records per-seed `retryMinutes` of **55 / 50 / 55** — a mean of
**53.3**, not 55.0. `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* consequently
quotes "55 of its 116.4 min (≈47 %)", pairing seed 1's retry total with the
mean total (the mean-based share is ≈45.8 %). `between sorties` and
`exposed re-capture` happen to be seed-invariant today, so only the retry line
is visibly wrong — but the rendering is one bug, not one line.

## Expected behaviour

Every metric line in the text report describes the same population (the seed
set), consistent with the JSON artefact: mean plus min–max for the per-run
totals, or an explicitly labelled seed-1 sample. The report-rendering test
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering*) should pin a
multi-seed case where the seeds differ, so the mixing cannot return.

## Acceptance criteria

- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the multi-seed aggregate (mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it), or labels them as a single seed; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.

# Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min against the authored 40–60 min window

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V (Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing
items), part of the re-measurement chain under AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A (Re-measure
ring timing for one-level hex deployments). **Producer ruling required** — this
item records the evidence and the options; it does not decide which way the
budget should move.

## Why this item exists

`RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors ring 1's grind window as **40–60 minutes** with a
±10 % tolerance of the window's width (**±2 minutes**), judged on the **grind**
line. The regenerated artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, produced
by `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` from the shipped code) measures the shipped one-level
five-wave sortie at **16.4 minutes**, so the authored window no longer holds.
The parent's acceptance criteria forbid silently re-wording a missed budget,
so the miss is recorded here and the ruling is left to the producer.

## Measurement (source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, ring 1, `grind`, seeds 1–3)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **missed** (`withinWindow: false`, `withinTolerance: false`) |
| Measured total mean | **16.4256 min** (seeds: 15.7239 / 16.6383 / 16.9144) |
| Measured total min–max | **15.7239 – 16.9144 min** |
| Authored window | **40 – 60 min** |
| Tolerance | ±10 % of window width = **±2 min** (tolerance floor 38 min) |
| Delta to window floor | **−23.5744 min** below 40 min; **−21.5744 min** below the 38 min tolerance floor |
| Deployment minutes (measured, mean) | 2.2128 (1.8619 / 2.3192 / 2.4572) |
| Between-sortie minutes (modelled) | 12.0 (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Retry minutes (measured replay) | 2.2128 (= the replayed deployment's measured length) |
| Re-capture minutes (modelled) | 0.0 (the grind line secures the ring) |
| Split check | 2.2128 + 12.0 + 2.2128 + 0.0 = 16.4256 = the total mean |
| Captured / lost sorties | 0.0 / **6.0** per run — every sortie is a first-attempt loss to enemy fire and is retried |
| Ring secured | 3 / 3 runs (the grind plays every hex, so the ring still ends secured) |
| Salvage | 0.0 banked, 15.0 forfeited (mean: 25 / 4 / 16) |

## Before/after attributable to the one-level model

| Ring 1 grind | Before (campaign slice) | After (one-level sortie) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total mean (min–max) | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | **16.4 (15.7–16.9)** | −37.9 min |
| Verdict | in-window (40–60) | **missed (40–60)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 19.0 | 2.2 | −16.8 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 23.3 | 2.2 | −21.1 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 12.0 | 12.0 | unchanged (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 4.7 | 0.0 / 6.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 24.0 / 54.0 | 0.0 / 15.0 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈0.4 min, and the retry term follows it
mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length). The
between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged and
do not drive the delta.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-1 window** (e.g. from 40–60 min to a window the shipped
   one-level model measures). Cheapest, but it changes the design of record
   (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape) rather than the game.
2. **Tune the authored ring data** — more hexes in ring 1, or higher
   aggression/level per hex — so a ring-1 clear takes the authored time. This
   changes gameplay pace, not the timing model.
3. **Revisit the allowances** — the between-sortie 2 minutes, the retry rule
   (one modelled replay per loss) and the rush re-capture charge. A larger
   between-sortie or retry allowance would lengthen the measured total, but it
   prices a deployment time the harness does not measure.
4. **Revisit the measurement boundary** — the per-level arena ignores the wave
   `shootEnabled` gate, so every sortie is lost to enemy fire and none is
   captured. Honouring the gate (or modelling the mini-boss encounter, also
   unmodelled) would raise captures and change the measured total; that is a
   harness/model decision (`AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` chain), not a budget re-word.

## Acceptance criteria

- The producer rules on one of the options (or another) and records the
  decision on this item; **no option is taken implicitly** by a later code or
  docs change.
- If the ruling re-authors the window, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the docs guards
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
  the quoted documents are updated together and the artifact re-judged.
- If the ruling tunes the ring data or the allowances, the artifact is
  regenerated with the documented command and the before/after evidence is
  recorded here.
- Whatever the ruling, ring 1's grind verdict is stated honestly (measured
  figure, window, delta) — never re-worded as passing.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — section/grouping pins; update
  position-only assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — describe the
  sectioned map surface

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the
  scene and its intel model this item re-lays-out.
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (completed, parent): reveal filter,
  CVD-safe ownership, coordinates on tiles, spatial arrows — the readability and
  navigation pass that precedes this structural one.
- **AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK** — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (completed): titled
  every line of the selected-hex intel. Its line titles are load-bearing for
  this item's `selected-hex` section and must not be disturbed.
- **AH-0MWEWYUAS002P7P9** — Renderer: CVD-safe labels, reveal filter, owned-hex
  selection (completed); **AH-0MWEWYVD7008PPQT** — Navigation: grid columns
  (completed): both pin renderer behaviour this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defence report rolled into the hex map (completed):
  source of the attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel now moved into
  `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5** — Assault defence report and reset announcement
  (completed): source of the `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner now grouped under
  `last-sortie`.
- **AH-0MWF0CWB7002MG2F** — Special-mission intel (completed): the `★ SPECIAL`
  tile tag whose detail-panel block lives in `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: bank a fixed post-win bonus (open): owns the
  `winBonusLine` whose presentation Q3 decides.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): the
  legibility baseline this item must not regress.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)

Keyword false positive: `AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU` (audio) matched on generic words
(`make`, `there`) and is not related to this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Clutter inversion.** More framing can add more visual noise than it removes;
  mitigation: a small fixed section count (4 + footer by default), one heading
  style, and the non-overlap/fit assertions as the guard.
- **Text reflow collisions.** Wrapped draw names and long assault arithmetic are
  the strings that collide at 960×540; mitigation: wrap widths inside each
  section rect plus the "no body text overdraws a tile" assertion.
- **Parity drift.** A scene-local tweak would break gym↔game parity; mitigation:
  all layout in `hexMap.ts`, with the existing equivalence assertions kept.
- **Test churn on positions.** Several suites assert coordinates indirectly;
  mitigation: pin sections structurally (`sections` registry) rather than by
  literal pixel offsets, and update only position-only assertions.
- **Scope creep** into a full visual redesign, new fonts, or tabbed navigation;
  such opportunities are recorded as new linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** headings are monospace text in the existing style (no new
  assets); **assumption:** the attract/demo traversal gains no new state, because
  every section is read-only like today's panels.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — How should the sections be delineated?**
  (a) Bordered, headed panels in fixed columns — every section has a frame, a
  heading and a bounded rect (recommended).
  (b) Headed bands with separator rules only — headings plus horizontal rules,
  no boxes, more breathing space over the map background.
  (c) Collapsible/tabbed sections — only one section expanded at a time, cutting
  on-screen text but adding interaction state and hidden information.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a frame per section is the most unambiguous
  distinction, needs no new interaction, and is directly assertable (rect +
  heading + non-overlap) by the existing scene/renderer tests.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** bordered, headed panels in fixed
  columns. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q2 (ANSWERED, producer chose (b)) — Which grouping taxonomy should the map use?**
  (a) Six sections: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX, ATTACK,
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
  (b) Four sections plus a footer: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX
  (intel **and** its attack row together), CONTROLS/LEGEND (recommended).
  (c) Keep today's regions and only add headings/separators to each.
  **Recommended:** (b) — it separates the three genuinely unlike kinds of
  information (war state, transient news, focused-hex detail) while keeping one
  hex's intel and attack row together, and it avoids the extra section that
  option (a) spends on material that is about the same focused hex.
  Research: the inventory in *Problem statement* comes from
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; the attack panel and the detail panel are both
  keyed by the focused hex (`model.attackDetails` / `displayedHexKey`), which is
  what makes (b) coherent.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (b)** four sections plus a controls footer,
  with the focused hex's intel and its attack row in one `selected-hex` section.
  Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q3 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — Should the banked win-bonus line be
  rendered as part of this item?**
  (a) Yes — render `model.winBonusLine` (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) inside
  LAST SORTIE (recommended).
  (b) No — leave it query-only and record it as deliberately out of scope.
  (c) Remove the unused line/model field entirely.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the line already exists and is tested through the query
  seam; without it the "what just happened" section silently omits a reward the
  player just earned, and it is a one-line addition to a section this item is
  already building.
  Research: `winBonusLine` is produced by `defenceReport.ts` and republished by
  `hexIntel.ts`; `hexMap.ts` never draws it and `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`
  is its only reader.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** render `model.winBonusLine` inside
  `last-sortie`. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q4 (recorded, not blocking) — Is a repo/gym search needed for the selected-hex
  line titles?** Answered by inspection of AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK: the titles
  (`ID:`, `STATE:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, …) are shipped and are treated as a
  fixed input here. Source: work item description + `hexIntel.ts` constants.

# Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset

## Problem statement

The hangar currently treats the **whole fleet as permanent**: a deployed ship is not consumed when a battle ends, and buying an upgrade does not arm it. The producer wants each deployed ship to be a **one-battle consumable** — the flown hull, its equipped starting weapons and modifiers, and their bought permanent levels are spent on **win or loss** — while owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Re-fitting a new ship must be quick, so **buying an upgrade should enable it immediately**, and a follow-on item will add saved ship configurations for one-action re-purchase.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** building and flying ships through the hex war.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because the salvage economy must now fund re-fitting after every sortie.

Example user stories:

- As a player, after a battle I want the ship I flew to be spent, so each sortie is a real commitment and losing one costs me the ship, not my whole collection.
- As a player, I want buying an upgrade to arm it immediately, so re-fitting a new ship takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.
- As a player, I want the owned items I did not fly to survive, so a bad run never erases my progress.
- As a player, I want to keep the free starter hull and starter weapon, so I can always deploy after a wipe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted. Every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned.
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases. The player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win).
- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout. This deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.
- Automated tests cover both outcome paths and the purchase paths through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity): win and loss consumption, starter-kit survival, un-flown owned items surviving, consumed items' level rows removed, no soft-lock with an empty loadout, demo mode not overwriting the player's war, and auto-enable plus refusal for hull/weapon/modifier.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the ship you flew is spent and you rebuild from the salvage you earned — and because buying an upgrade now arms it immediately, re-fitting a new ship takes fewer steps and each sortie feels like a real commitment.

## Constraints

- **No soft-lock.** The free starter hull (`hull-1`) and starter weapon (`spread`) are always owned; an empty loadout is legal (deploy with the ship's permanent cannon only, AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D).
- **One payload write per battle** through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; defensive parsing stays the authority; no schema-version bump expected because the shape is unchanged.
- **Demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war** — the existing `_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard must keep holding for the consumed payload.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The consumption rule lives in the pure core and is exercised by the headless harness; no scene-only logic.
- **Supersedes a prior decision.** `hangarEconomy.buy()` currently documents that "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job" (A5/A6). This item overrides that for the hangar screen only.
- **Separate concern left alone.** The ring-end hangar-falls reset (`resetCampaign`, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) already wipes both axes and is unchanged.
- **No new balance tuning.** The existing win bonus (`bankWinBonus` / `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`) already provides the "wins pay more" difference the producer described.

## Existing state

- `buy()` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` spends the price and adds the entry to the owned set, but deliberately does **not** equip it.
- `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` in `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` clone the payload and currently **preserve** `hangar.activeHull` and `hangar.activeLoadout`.
- `HangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) already carries the deployed `hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers` and the carried war `payload`, so the scene has the ship identity at battle end.
- `parseHangar` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) restores `activeHull` / `activeLoadout`; `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter hull and starter weapon as owned, not equipped.
- Permanent levels live in `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels`.
- Precedent: `resolveHexCapture` already derives the hex's defending bot from the deployed hull (`leaveDefender`), so "the flown hull is spent" fits the existing capture model.

## Desired change

- Add a **pure consumption reducer** (for example `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue)`) that removes the flown hull, equipped starting weapons and modifiers plus their level rows, resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout`, and preserves the starter kit and every un-flown owned item.
- Apply it on **both** the win path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the loss path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), driven by the deployment's hull and the hangar's active loadout.
- Add **auto-enable on purchase** to the hangar purchase path (`purchaseHangarEntry` / `buy` with an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option), keeping `buy`'s default non-equipping behaviour for other callers.
- Update the hangar screen so a purchase reads as equipped immediately, and update the affected unit/integration tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — add the pure `consumeDeployedShip` reducer and an `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; keep the default non-equipping for other callers.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — consume on the `resolveHexCapture` win path and the `resolveDeploymentDefeat` loss path; thread the deployed ship into both.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — expose the exact equipped set (hull + active loadout) that consumption applies to.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the deployment's hull/loadout into the capture and defeat resolvers.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `purchaseHangarEntry` uses `equipOnPurchase` and renders the auto-equipped state immediately.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — persist the auto-equipped purchase through the same payload write.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — confirm the consumed/auto-equipped payload round-trips; no schema bump expected.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Economy treadmill.** Consuming the flown ship every battle could feel punitive, especially after a loss. Mitigation: wins pay more salvage (existing bonus), and the saved-configuration follow-on (AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7) makes re-fitting one action; validate against the ring-timing budgets before advancing.
- **Soft-lock.** Consumption must never remove the starter kit or leave no deployable ship. Mitigation: always retain `hull-1` and `spread`, and keep the empty-loadout rule (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D); test it.
- **Silent loss of un-flown levels.** Removing level rows must target only the deployed ids. Mitigation: consume the resolved deployed ids only, and assert un-flown `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows survive.
- **Split writes.** Consumption, banking and the win bonus must land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write. Mitigation: pure reducer plus a single persist, with a test that the balance and ownership cannot diverge.
- **Demo leakage.** An attract/demo run must never consume the player's war. Mitigation: the existing demo guard on `_saveHangarWarPayload`; test it.
- **Scope creep.** Auto-enable could grow into a full loadout-preset system; that is deliberately split into AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7. Price, win-bonus and ring-economy tuning stay out of scope.
- **Stale loadout references.** A save whose active loadout names items no longer owned is already filtered by `resolveActiveLoadout`; consumption must operate on resolved ids, not raw stored ids.

**Assumptions:** both outcomes consume the ship (Q2 = B); only deployed items are consumed (Q4 = B); the ring-end hangar-falls reset is unchanged; and "the ship" is the hangar's active loadout as shown, not the six-slot post-cap run set.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6** — Capture cycle: hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (the win path this item extends).
- **AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I** — Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment (the deployment payload this item consumes).
- **AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J** — Capture-cycle assault gate (the ring-end hangar-falls reset; deliberately unchanged).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ** — Strengthen a hex's defence (a nearby economy change to co-ordinate with).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (empty-loadout legality this item must preserve).
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** — Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (the follow-on created from this intake; depends on this item).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D persistence rules), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (capture cycle), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWB8VFBC003743Y** – Requote docs and reconcile ring-timing guards (completed)
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** – Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (blocked)
- **AH-0MWB8VDDI005WVMG** – Pin per-ring loadout resolution in tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+28 more)
- `README.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+27 more)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: battle, build, cores, defend, earned (+25 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What should the hangar show after a hex battle (win or loss)?** — Answer (producer): **C, refined** — the deployed ship is genuinely consumed on both outcomes and **all its upgrades must be re-purchased**; when an upgrade is purchased it is **automatically enabled**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 follow-on — add saved ship configurations?** — Answer (producer): **yes** — save ship configurations and select them from a drop-down to quickly purchase the needed upgrades. Created as **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Should winning and losing differ?** — Answer (producer): **B** — winning also consumes the deployed hull (it is left as the hex's defender); losing destroys it. The difference is economic: a win pays more salvage to equip a new ship. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Bug or design change?** — Answer (producer): **B** — this is a design-change request, not a defect report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — After a hex battle, how much of the fleet must be re-purchased?** — Answer (producer): **B** — only the deployed ship is consumed: its equipped hull, equipped weapons, equipped modifiers and their levels are removed; owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Source: interactive reply.

**Assumptions carried:** the free starter hull and starter weapon are always owned (no soft-lock); un-equip toggles remain available after an auto-equip; and the existing win bonus already supplies the "wins pay more" difference, so no new balance tuning is in scope.

## Traceability

- Duplicate check performed — no open or completed item covers ship consumption on battle completion; the closest items are the capture-cycle, assault-gate and defender items listed above, which this item extends rather than duplicates.

Add **saved ship configurations** to the hangar:

- The player can save a named build — the hull, the equipped starting weapons and the equipped modifiers (including the permanent levels the build relies on).

- A build whose salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the shortfall (which entries/minerals/cores are missing) rather than partially applying or silently failing.
- Saving, renaming and deleting builds are part of the surface; a saved build survives a war reset only if the design says it should (see the parent item's persistence rule).

# Goal

As a player, I want one pure, reusable rule that spends exactly the ship I flew, so the hangar can reflect a battle's outcome without any scene owning a copy of the consumption logic.

## Context

Core slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q4 = B: only the deployed ship is consumed — equipped hull, equipped starting weapons, equipped modifiers and their bought permanent levels; un-flown owned items and the free starter kit survive). Gym↔game parity means this lives in the pure core, never in a scene.

## Scope

- Add `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue?)` to `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`, beside `equipHull`/`equipLoadout`, with a `DeployedShip` shape (`{ hullId, startingWeapons, modifiers }`) shared with the capture cycle (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`).
- Removes the flown hull from `unlockedHulls` (unless it is the free starter hull `hull-1`), each equipped starting weapon from `unlockedWeapons` (unless it is the free starter weapon `spread`), and each equipped modifier from `ownedModifiers`.
- Deletes only the consumed ids' rows from `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`; every un-flown id's row and the `bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores` balances are untouched.
- Resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout` (both lists empty), so a deployment still builds with only the ship's permanent cannon.
- Pure and total: the input hangar is never mutated, unknown/stale ids are ignored, a repeated call on an already-consumed hangar is idempotent, and no throw is possible from a corrupt save.
- Contract unit tests beside the module: hull/weapon/modifier removal, starter survival, un-flown survival, level-row pruning (both kinds), balance invariance, empty-loadout result, idempotence, purity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `consumeDeployedShip` is exported from the hangar economy module (and its types from `types.ts`), documented with a doc comment that names this parent item.
- On a hangar that owns a starter kit plus a bought hull/weapon/modifier with permanent levels, consuming a deployed ship removes exactly the flown ids and their level rows, keeps every other owned id and row, keeps both balances, sets `activeHull` to the starter hull and empties `activeLoadout`.
- Deploying the starter hull and the starter weapon never removes them, and the resulting hangar is still deployable (a deployment payload builds with an empty loadout).
- Calling it twice with the same ship yields the same hangar as calling it once (idempotent), and the caller's hangar object is unchanged after both calls.
- Unit tests cover every bullet above, including an unknown hull/weapon/modifier id and a modifier/weapon with no level row.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green.

- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts — `consumeDeployedShip`, beside `equipHull`/`equipLoadout`

- Depends on: the acceptance-tests item (its contract is the definition of done)
- Blocks: the battle-end wiring item

The hangar now has one auditable rule for what a sortie costs, so a win and a loss can never spend different amounts of the player's fleet.

# Goal

As a player, after a hex battle I want the ship I flew to be spent — win or loss — so each sortie is a real commitment and a bad run costs me the ship, not my collection.

## Context

The gameplay slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q2 = B: a win leaves the hull as the hex's defender and still spends it; a loss destroys it; the difference is economic — a win pays more salvage). Today both resolvers clone the payload and **preserve** the equipped ship, and the defeat path persists nothing at all.

## Scope

- Thread the flown ship into the pure capture cycle: `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` take the deployment's `DeployedShip` (hull + active loadout as flown), falling back to the hangar's own resolved `activeHull` / `resolveActiveLoadout` when a caller passes none.
- Apply `consumeDeployedShip` on the **win** path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the **loss** path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), after the salvage settlement/banking so consumption can never change a balance, and after `leaveDefender` so the defending bot still derives from the flown hull.
- A `campaignReset` (ring-end hangar falls, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) still returns the freshly reset campaign — the reset wins over consumption.
- `PlayScene`: pass `this.hangarWarDeployment`'s hull and loadout into both calls, and make the loss path persist the consumed payload through the existing demo-guarded `_saveHangarWarPayload` so ownership, banking and the win bonus land in **one** write per battle. `_forfeitUnbankedSalvage` currently writes nothing.
- Keep the demo/attract guard intact: an attract run must never write the consumed payload over the player's war.
- Gym↔game parity: the headless seam (`GymHexWar.captureHex` and the pure resolvers) exercises the same code; no scene-only rule.
- Update the module doc comments that state "losing a run never loses the hangar" to the new rule (the flown ship is spent; the hangar and ring otherwise persist).

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a winning deployment the payload has the flown hull (unless starter), flown starting weapons (unless starter), flown modifiers and their level rows removed; `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty; the win bonus and the banked salvage still land; exactly one payload write happens.
- After a losing deployment the same consumption happens and the payload is persisted exactly once through the demo-guarded write; only the salvage earned since the last bank is forfeited, and the balances are otherwise unchanged by consumption.
- Owned items the player did not fly, their permanent level rows and the free starter kit survive both paths; the post-battle hangar is deployable with an empty loadout (no soft-lock).
- A ring-end `campaignReset` outcome is byte-identical to today's reset payload (consumption does not apply on top of the reset).
- Demo mode (`demoMode` true) leaves the stored `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload untouched on both paths.
- The acceptance tests for consumption (parent test item) go green, and the resolver suites (`captureCycle.test.ts`) plus `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` pass.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green.

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted; every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned. (Restated from the parent item.)
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases; the player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win). (Restated from the parent item.)

## Key Files

- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts — `resolveHexCapture` (win) and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` (loss) apply the reducer; module/rule doc comments updated
- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — win/loss consumption, campaignReset and refusal-path coverage
- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts — pass the deployment's ship into both resolvers; persist the loss payload once (`_forfeitUnbankedSalvage`, `_saveHangarWarPayload`)
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts — expose the exact flown set (`hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers`) as the `DeployedShip`
- src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts — parity: the gym capture runs the same consuming resolver
- src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts — end-to-end battle-end ownership assertions

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF
- Depends on: the pure reducer item and the acceptance-tests item
- Unchanged by design: AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J (ring-end hangar-falls reset), AH-0MWHF71UG000LI6W (defender upgrade snapshot)

## Impact

Every hex battle now costs the ship you flew, so sorties feel like commitments and the salvage you earn is visibly what funds the next ship.

# Goal

As a player, I want a purchase to arm the part immediately, so re-fitting a new ship after a lost sortie takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.

## Context

The economy slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q1 = C refined: "when an upgrade is purchased it is automatically enabled"). Today `buy()` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) documents and implements "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job (A5/A6)". This item deliberately supersedes that rule **for the hangar screen only**, while other callers keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.

## Scope

- Add an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option to `buy(hangar, entry, context, options?)`, default **off** so every existing caller (attract/demo decision, tests, gyms) keeps the documented non-equipping behaviour.
- When on and the purchase succeeds: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers` — each deduplicated. A refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership, balance nor loadout.
- `purchaseHangarEntry` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) opts in, so every hangar-screen purchase lands owned **and** equipped in the same payload.
- `HangarScene` persists the auto-equipped payload through the same single `saveHangarWarPayload` write it already uses, and the screen model (`buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen`) shows the purchased row as equipped/subscribed (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`) on the next render without a second render pass or a hint.
- Keep the un-equip toggles (`equipHangarHull`, `toggleHangarWeapon`, `toggleHangarModifier`) available after an auto-equip — the player can always put a part back on the bench.
- Update the doc comments that state the A5/A6 "buying never equips" rule so they name the hangar-screen opt-in.
- Tests: pure `buy` with and without the option, all three entry kinds, every refusal path, `purchaseHangarEntry` payload result, and the screen model rendering the equipped state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buy(..., { equipOnPurchase: true })` equips a purchased hull (`activeHull`), weapon (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`) and modifier (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and returns the spent price unchanged from today's behaviour.
- `buy(...)` without the option behaves exactly as today (ownership only) — pinned by a test so the A5/A6 contract cannot silently drift for other callers.
- A refused purchase with `equipOnPurchase: true` leaves ownership, balance and loadout identical to before the call (deep-equal payload).
- `purchaseHangarEntry` equips on success and persists nothing on refusal; the screen model built from the resulting payload renders the row as equipped (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`).
- An auto-equipped part can still be un-equipped through the existing toggle functions, and an empty loadout stays legal.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green, and the auto-enable acceptance tests go green.

- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout; this deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option. (Restated from the parent item.)

## Key Files

- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts — `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; doc comments naming the supersession
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts — option/refusal/kind coverage
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts — `purchaseHangarEntry` opts in; model/renderer equipped state
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarSlice.integration.test.ts — screen-model evidence of the equipped purchase
- src/scenes/HangarScene.ts — persist the auto-equipped payload in the same write
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts — doc comment on the "owning never equips" default that now applies only to callers that do not opt in

- Parent: AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF
- Depends on: the acceptance-tests item
- Supersedes for this screen: the A5/A6 "buying only grants ownership" rule
- Follow-on: AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7 (saved ship configurations re-purchase a known build in one action)

Buying a part now arms it, so rebuilding a ship after a lost sortie is a handful of clicks rather than a buy-then-equip hunt.
